title: Assessing Human Competence in an Age of AI Augmentation
summary: Just as swimming and canoeing test different kinds of mastery, recognizing performance expanded by AI requires assessment suited to changing capabilities and conditions. A good result produced with AI has value, but it cannot by itself tell us what a person learned or how they exercised judgment. Drawing on learning research and the autoformalization of mathematical proofs, this review examines that distinction and proposes assessment criteria that recognize both learning and augmented performance.
